findings.title: Lethal trifecta: untrusted input + private data + external sink
findings.detail: Server "govern" exposes tools that together enable an exfiltration flow. Untrusted content: audit_mcp_config, audit_skill_file, injection_scan, agent_readiness_scan · Private data: audit_mcp_config, scope_check, audit_skill_file, injection_scan, governance_policy · Public sink: injection_scan · Destructive: audit_mcp_config, scope_check, audit_skill_file.

evidence.snippet: Untrusted content: audit_mcp_config, audit_skill_file, injection_scan, agent_readiness_scan · Private data: audit_mcp_config, scope_check, audit_skill_file, injection_scan, governance_policy · Public sink: injection_scan · Destructive: audit_mcp_config, scope_check, audit_skill_file

findings.remediation: Do not co-install these capabilities under one trust boundary; an injected comment/email can steer the model to exfiltrate via the sink tool.

findings.title: Tool description changed since last scan
findings.detail: Tool "audit_mcp_config" changed its description with no version change. Silent description changes are how a trusted server turns malicious after review.
